c1.sql:
WITH b AS (SELECT item, retailer, channel, price_zar FROM analyst.retail_prices WHERE day='2026-11-14'),
m AS (SELECT item, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY price_zar) med, min(price_zar) mn, count(*) nret FROM b GROUP BY item)
SELECT b.retailer AS "Retailer", b.channel AS "Channel", count(*) AS "Shared items", round(avg(100*b.price_zar/m.med)::numeric,0) AS "Index vs item median", round(avg(100*(b.price_zar-m.mn)/m.mn)::numeric,0) AS "Gap to cheapest %", sum(CASE WHEN b.price_zar=m.mn THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Items cheapest"
FROM b JOIN m USING(item) WHERE nret>=2 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 4
c1.title: Woolworths prices 14% below the item median; Makro 26% above
c1.subtitle: Price index = 100 × retailer price ÷ median price of the same item that day; 14 Nov 2026, 24 items with 2+ retailers

steps: Price sections (1, 2, 4, 5, 6) use analyst.retail_prices, retail_unit_prices and retail_price_changes for 2026-11-01 to 2026-12-01 (exclusive). The only day available is 14 Nov 2026, when collection started, so it is treated as the baseline.

Indexes: 100 × price ÷ the median price of the same item that day, averaged per retailer and per channel, over the 24 items priced by 2+ retailers. Gap to cheapest = price ÷ the item's lowest price − 1.

The like-for-like basket uses the items priced by all of Woolworths, Superb Hyper and Clicks on 14 Nov (3 items). Sixty60 vs Shoprite uses their 5 shared items. Spreads are dearest ÷ cheapest − 1 per item.
Outliers were audited in analyst.retail_offers (titles and price vs item median) and flagged rather than removed.

The demand section uses analyst.search_interest, groups 'retail: specials by retailer · 12 months' and 'marketplace: online shopping · 12 months': monthly averages of weekly values for June to November 2026 (November = weeks of 1 and 8 Nov). Weeks from Nov–Dec 2025 are used only as the seasonal-peak reference.
trust: Every price compares the same item at different retailers on the same day, with brand and size title-matching and a 0.5–2× median filter.
Search-trend directions are consistent week to week (e.g. Black Friday 2, 3, 5, 8, 14, 20 from October to November).
Known-value items (milk, chocolate, washing powder) show tight, believable spreads.
limits: No change within the month, promotions or momentum can be measured until a second price day exists. There are no price data before 14 Nov 2026.
The house-brand gap cannot be measured: 0 house-brand rows and empty unit prices on 14 Nov.
Search interest is relative within each group, and November is partial (to 8 Nov). Do not compare raw values across groups.

risks: Single-day snapshot: positions may reflect one-day specials rather than everyday prices.
Thin overlap: retailer indexes rest on 6–12 items and the like-for-like basket on 3 items.
Pack-size and variant mismatches (Makro Pampers, Shoprite Domestos combo, Clicks Vaseline variant) inflate some spreads and indexes.
These are online advertised prices, not till prices. Pick n Pay and SPAR had no matching prices on 14 Nov.
Search-trend data is relative and November covers only 2 weeks.
actions: 1. Lock in 14 Nov as the pre-Black Friday reference and run 7-day and month-end price comparisons on 21 Nov and 1 Dec.
2. Have Black Friday promo prices and stock live by 23 Nov, the week of last year's search peak, especially at SPAR and Shoprite where specials searches are rising.
3. Audit known-value items (Clover milk, Cadbury, Omo) daily, because any retailer breaking the 0–7% spread will be visible to shoppers.
4. Review household and personal care pricing where spreads are 39–56% (Sunlight, Simba, Shield), and agree promo guardrails with the retailers at the low end.
5. Add house-brand equivalents and fix pack-size matching (nappies, bleach, lotion) so that December can report the house-brand gap and clean spreads.
6. Track the Sixty60 vs Shoprite premium weekly. If it rises above 11%, check whether quick-commerce pricing is hurting conversion.
findings: The November edition rests on one baseline day (14 Nov 2026): 88 like-for-like prices, 37 items, 9 retailers.
Woolworths indexed 86 and was cheapest on 5 of 9 items. Makro (126) and Takealot (120) were dearest.
Grocery chains indexed 96 and online marketplaces 110, a 14-point channel gap.
The median price spread for the same item was 38%. Household and personal care spread widest, while milk, Cadbury and Omo spread 0–7%.
Checkers Sixty60 cost 11% more than Shoprite on 5 shared items.
Black Friday searches reached 20 against last year's peak of 100 (week of 23 Nov 2025). SPAR specials rose 36% and Shoprite specials 15% from October to November.
